assets.title: Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature
assets.credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio
assets.legend: Flow lines coloured by modelled sea surface temperature: blue 0 C, green 10-20 C, yellow about 25 C, red 32 C. Colorbar file: sst_ecco2_cbar.png
limitations: Model output, not observation.
Flow lines are a rendering; values between model grid points are interpolated.
Equirectangular map: pixel scale varies with latitude.
Covers one modelled year; not a climate trend.

assets.title: Perpetual Ocean 2: Western Boundary Currents
assets.role: rejected as first input; possible context
assets.legend: Beauty version: flows surface to 600 m white; deeper flows blue-cyan-white (about -3 to 22 C). Separate temperature and salinity versions exist.
limitations: Camera moves: rotating globe, zooms to Kuroshio, Agulhas, Gulf Stream. Optical flow would measure the camera.
Beauty colours encode depth, chosen for appearance.
Particle trails are 3-day (above 600 m) and 6-day (deeper).

assets.title: GEOS Aerosols (2025)
assets.role: second source (approved by Dev A, 15 Nov), one still
assets.eic_gallery: Not in the Earth Information Center gallery (checked 2026-11-15: the gallery does not list 5669, and the 5669 page links to no gallery). Listed as 'GEOS Aerosols' in the challenge's resource list, separate from the EIC Content Database item. TO CONFIRM (Mr. E): the challenge page's GEOS Aerosols link goes to svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5669. Do not call it EIC data.
assets.credit: NASA's Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) and NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS)
assets.legend: Aerosol type: blue sea salt, pink/magenta dust, orange/red smoke from fires, green sulfates from pollution and volcanoes. Colour bar file: Aerosols_cbar.png

map_geometry.checked: lon/lat grid on the still: 0 line passes the UK and the Ghana coast, 60N meets Greenland's southern tip, Antarctica from about 70S

limitations: Model output (GEOS-FP replay), not an observation.
One moment only (19 Aug 2025 20:00 UTC): no change over time, so each region plays a steady rhythm.
Plumes are a rendering of modelled aerosol; the numbers describe the drawn picture, not air quality or amounts.
Pixels are not square (16:9 world map): 0.094 degrees per pixel east-west, 0.083 north-south.
